messages:
sam: quick sync — throwing up a guardrail idea for discussion. proposal: block org-scoped wildcard API keys from being used by service workloads by default. require either project-scoped keys or an explicit admin whitelist for org-scoped use.
lara: can you sketch the threat model you want to mitigate? is this more about blast radius (exfil) or accidental cross-tenant access? :thinking:
sam: mostly blast radius + accidental misuse. we've seen infra jobs accidentally pick up org keys in sandboxing tests. org keys leak -> everything accessible. jun: strong 👍 for reducing blast radius. but this might break some CI flows that rely on org tokens. how do we migrate? matt: we should keep a temporary escape hatch: an allowlist for service principals plus audit logging and a 30-day deprecation window. no permanent wildcard keys in runtime unless recorded in allowlist.
sam: exactly. migration plan: 1) deny by default at runtime 2) provide allowlist and audit logs 3) implement linting in deploy pipeline to catch uses 4) roll deprecation notices to owners.
jun: runtime deny — is this enforced at token validation layer or at gateway? I prefer gateway enforcement so we can centralize metrics and rollout. auth-bot: policy applied: token_scope_policy=v1 deny-org-wildcard unless allowlist entry exists.
lara: gateway is fine. but we need the semantics: how do we detect "wildcard"? key metadata like scopes: ["*"], or a field is_org_scoped=true + no per-project binding. keep it deterministic. matt: also consider operator flows where org keys are used for admin tasks. allowlist should be limited to human-managed ops services (not user pods).
jun: follow-up: do we change API key creation UX? show a warning when creating org-scoped keys recommending project keys for runtime. also add TTL enforcement on org keys by default.
sam: UX + defaults are key. devex can add a checkbox: "allow runtime use by services (unsafe)" that auto-creates an allowlist ticket.
lara: note on RBAC: if we require project-scoped keys for services, we need a mapping mechanism so service identity can assume project-level roles across multiple projects safely. that's an infra effort.
matt: agree — propose an "assume-project" broker pattern: service uses short-lived project token obtained from broker after proving identity. broker ACLs control which projects can be assumed. reduces need for many long-lived keys.
jun: sounds good. small nit: how will tracing look? we should propagate origin key id and broker-assumed-project in traces for audit.
sam: summary: we have consensus on deny-by-default for org wildcard keys, gateway enforcement, allowlist/escapes with audit, UX nudges, and a broker pattern long-term. next step: i'll draft a short RFC with migration plan and a checklist for platform teams. can ppl ack if they can review the RFC this week?
lara: can review.
jun: can review Friday.
matt: can review.
auth-bot: note: created ticket INFRA-4921 to track broker PoC and audit pipeline work.
